profile.reading:
DataBank IAD4 sits at 21625 Red Rum Drive, Ashburn, Virginia, the newest of three DataBank buildings on the company's Ashburn campus. DataBank announced IAD4's groundbreaking on July 25, 2024, with Data Center Dynamics coverage quoting DataBank CEO Raul K. Martynek the following day; the facility is being built in collaboration with GI Partners, which is leasing the full two-story building to DataBank. DataBank's own materials state IAD4 will offer 70,000 square feet of IT space and 20 megawatts of critical IT load with 17 onsite network carriers, using DataBank's "Universal Data Hall Design" intended to support both traditional enterprise workloads and high-performance computing and AI workloads, with N+1 power and cooling and a 100 percent renewable energy sourcing claim. DataBank's own press release targets Q1 2026 for availability; third-party trade press coverage separately referenced a Q2 2025 construction-completion date alongside the Q1 2026 availability date in the same article, a gap this profile notes rather than resolves, since DataBank's own release commits only to the Q1 2026 figure. DataBank does not name the power utility for IAD4, though Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record. Across the full three-building Ashburn campus, DataBank states 355,330 square feet of IT space and 69.9 megawatts of critical IT load on 18 acres, backed by roughly 70 megawatts of utility substation power. Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors and Fairfax County have both taken up data center-specific zoning and environmental-review measures in recent years as the region's buildout has accelerated, including Fairfax County's September 2024 Data Centers Zoning Ordinance Amendment.

DataBank's GI Partners collaboration on IAD4 reflects a broader industry pattern of data center operators partnering with real estate investment firms to fund new hyperscale-adjacent capacity while retaining operational control; GI Partners has separately backed data center real estate across multiple U.S. markets. Ashburn's Data Center Alley has driven repeated Dominion Energy transmission and generation investment cited in the utility's integrated resource plans and periodic Virginia State Corporation Commission rate cases, as regional demand, including DataBank's Ashburn campus, has become the single largest driver of the utility's near-term capital spending in its Virginia service territory.

Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 97 (DataBank): operator own Northern Virginia market page gave a full address, IT capacity, and sqft for a previously address-less row, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own Northern Virginia market overview page, fetched this session, describes this facility as IAD4, on the Ashburn Campus, and gives its address as 21625 Red Rum Drive, Ashburn, VA 20147, with 20 MW of critical IT load and 70,000 IT square feet.

reading.body:
IAD4 is the newest building on DataBank's three-facility Ashburn campus, scheduled for Q1 2026 availability with 20 megawatts of critical IT load across 70,000 square feet of IT space. The campus operator describes the facility as capable of supporting both traditional enterprise and high-performance computing workloads, with N+1 power and cooling and a stated commitment to 100 percent renewable energy sourcing. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 20 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 500 racks, though DataBank does not publish tenant composition or accelerator counts.

DataBank does not name the utility serving IAD4, but Dominion Energy operates as the public utility for Loudoun County where the facility sits. The full Ashburn campus totals 69.9 megawatts across three buildings on 18 acres, backed by roughly 70 megawatts of utility substation capacity, making the campus itself a material load point within Dominion's near-term capital spending drivers for its Virginia service territory. The facility ranks outside the top 20 published-capacity data centers in Virginia, though Virginia's 326 mapped facilities include 23 with published megawatt figures totaling 1,375.4 megawatts statewide.

Fairfax County and Loudoun County have both enacted data center-specific zoning and environmental-review measures in recent years as regional buildout has accelerated, creating local regulatory context for facility siting. IAD4 is being developed by DataBank in partnership with GI Partners, a real estate investor backing the full two-story building under a lease arrangement to DataBank, reflecting an industry pattern of separating real estate ownership from operational control in new capacity builds.
